name: Looking for a Place to Happen

podcast.body: From "Fully Completely," this song features a lyrical dexterity where Gord Downie manages to rhyme "Jacques Cartier." "In looking for a place to happen, Gord finds a way to rhyme Jacques Carcay."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: This song explores Canadian history through its lyrics, featuring a lyrical reference to Jacques Cartier, the French explorer credited with claiming Canada for France in 1534. Gord Downie's lyrical delivery shifts perspective, embodying a colonial explorer in the initial two verses, and then adopting the viewpoint of a First Nations person in the third verse, lamenting the arrival and encroachment of Europeans. "Gord Downey seems to assume the role of a colonial explorer in the first two verses. But then he reverts to the viewpoint of a First Nations person in verse 3 in which he laments the arrival and the encroachment of Europeans."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Tragically Hip's Fully Completely Reissue With Rob Baker
